newsitem.title: GREECE: UPDATE: GREEK FARMERS PROTEST GROWS, MORE ROADBLOCKS.
newsitem.headline: UPDATE: GREEK FARMERS PROTEST GROWS, MORE ROADBLOCKS.

text.p: Greek farmers extended a blockade of national road and rail links on Monday, cutting off more farm areas on the fifth day of their protest and sparking warnings of fresh-food shortages in the capital.
They showed no sign of backing down in their showdown with the ruling socialists despite numerous government pleas to call off their action which is causing transport chaos.
More than 20 roadblocks, made up of thousands of colourful tractors and piles of burning tyres, have been positioned around Greece to choke off almost all transport on main roads.
"We see major problems with fresh produce supplies at Athens central market from tomorrow (Tuesday)," said Dimitris Poulis, president of the giant market's produce importers.
Thanasis Markou, president of the market's meat importers, said if the protest continued into next week, then prices would rise dramatically.
A similar farmers' protest in 1995 lasted 10 days, sent food prices soaring and cost the economy tens of millions of dollars.

Reinforcements arrived at the farmers' roadside camps in the eastern Thessaly farm region on Monday and new blockades went up near Arta in western Greece and the Macedonia and Thrace regions of northern Greece above Salonika.
Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tsoumakas told reporters the government would announce decisions on how to handle the dispute later on Monday. Farmers have rejected several proposals.
The farmers want lower fuel costs, lower Value Added Tax (VAT) on farm equipment, higher price supports -- especially for cotton -- and rescheduling $1.3 billion in debts at state banks.

Barricades have now road links to Ioannina in the northwest, the western port of Patras which services Italy, the eastern mainland towns of Larissa, Karditsa, Volos and Trikola, and the northern towns of Drama and Kavala.

Police reported minor clashes between international truckers coming from Italy and farmers at the Patras barricades. Convoys of trapped commercial trucks, stretching more than a kilometre, now line Greece's national highways.
Farmers also gathered around the international airport at Salonika, the second city and main northern port, and threatened to seal off its access roads.

The protest began on Thursday by cutting all main road and rail links between Athens and Salonika. Farmers drove 5,000 tractors onto the motorway in the Thessaly farm region around the town of Larissa.
Bonfires of tyres lit up the night. Despite bitter cold and rain, the farmers were in a festive mood, setting up quarters on the motorways with chairs, tables and plastic tent shelters.

Local musicians mingled with the boisterous farmers, singing folk songs to loud cheers and applause. Roadside catering trucks fed the farmers, many of whom have arrived by bus to support the protestors.
Banners proclaiming "Don't Give In" hung from overpasses and tractors flew black flags of protest or the blue and white Greek flag. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
